source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: How should the nurse speak to an older adult with age-related hearing loss?
questions.rationale: Speak distinctly in a normal tone and face the client; shouting and high pitch make hearing harder.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Care of the elderly (PDF p. 5)
questions.quote: Speak distinctly, clearly, using normal tone of voice. DO NOT SHOUT.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An older adult has more trouble hearing his granddaughter than his son. This is because aging first affects hearing of:
questions.rationale: Presbycusis causes loss of high-pitched sounds first; low-pitched tones are heard more easily.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Special senses (PDF p. 5)
questions.quote: low pitched tones are heard more easily

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which nursing action best maintains an older client's self-esteem?
options: Let him do as much as he safely can
Do all his hygiene for him
Set a strict schedule for him
questions.rationale: Self-esteem is supported by encouraging independence within his abilities, with safety maintained.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Promoting independence (PDF p. 5)
questions.quote: Encourage the client to do as much as possible for himself/herself, provided that safety is maintained.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which skin care measure is appropriate for an older adult?
options: Give a full bath every day
questions.rationale: Aging skin is dry; use mild superfatted soap and lotion, avoid alcohol, and alternate sponge and full baths.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Hygiene and skin care (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: Use mild, superfatted soap to promote moisture of the skin.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Before trimming an older adult's thick toenails, the nurse should:
options: Soak the feet in warm water
questions.rationale: Soaking softens the hard nails, making cutting easier and preventing trauma.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Hygiene and skin care (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: Soak feet in warm water before cutting nails. The nails are usually hard.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: An older adult's temperature rises from his usual 36.4 °C to 37.2 °C and he is newly confused. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Older adults run lower temperatures and rarely mount high fever; a slight rise and new confusion often signal infection, especially UTI or respiratory.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Regulation of body temperature (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: Confusion is a common sign of infection, especially in the urinary tract.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: To prevent orthostatic hypotension, an older client is taught to:
questions.rationale: Gradual position change lets reflexes adapt; also keep adequate fluids, avoid straining and avoid sudden bending.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Exercise and body alignment (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: Practice gradual change of position to prevent orthostatic hypotension.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: An older client wakes often at night to void. Which advice helps?
options: Stop all fluids for the day
questions.rationale: Limiting fluids before bed reduces nocturia; avoid caffeine and long naps; keep daytime fluids adequate.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Promotion of sleep (PDF p. 7)
questions.quote: Limit fluid intake of the client before going to bed.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which dietary advice suits a healthy older adult?
questions.rationale: Lower metabolic rate means fewer calories; protein, fiber and fluids prevent constipation and support health.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Nutritional needs (PDF p. 7)
questions.quote: Increase protein in diet, but reduce calories. The metabolic rate of the elderly is slowed.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why are older adults prone to constipation?
options: Slower GI motility and low intake
questions.rationale: Aging brings decreased motility, appetite, thirst and intake, raising the tendency to constipation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Gastrointestinal system (PDF p. 4)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why do older adults need lower drug doses for many medications?
questions.rationale: Reduced renal and liver function slow elimination and metabolism, raising blood levels and toxicity risk.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Aging and medications (PDF p. 8)
questions.quote: Decrease in renal function, resulting in slower elimination of drugs

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Fat-soluble drugs stay longer in older adults because aging increases:
questions.rationale: A higher fat-to-lean ratio retains fat-soluble drugs and increases toxicity potential.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Aging and medications (PDF p. 8)
questions.quote: Increased proportion of fat to lean body mass, which facilitates retention of fat soluble drugs

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: An 80-year-old shares his life stories with satisfaction and gives advice to grandchildren. He has achieved:
questions.rationale: Ego integrity: viewing life with satisfaction and sharing wisdom; fear of death and regret indicate despair.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Answers and rationales (PDF p. 11)
questions.quote: An elderly has achieved Ego Integrity when he views life with satisfaction and shares his wisdom.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A 56-year-old woman with osteoporosis says something that needs correction. Which?
questions.rationale: Excess caffeine increases calcium loss; skim milk, weight-bearing walks and proper lifting are correct.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Answers and rationales (PDF p. 12)
questions.quote: Too much caffeine causes loss of calcium from the body.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is the most helpful approach for a client with dementia?
options: Reorient to person, time and place often
Leave him alone for long periods
questions.rationale: Dementia is mainly memory loss; frequent reorientation and a consistent routine help.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Answers and rationales (PDF p. 12)
questions.quote: reorient him to people, time, place and schedule of activities

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An older adult is at higher risk for infection mainly because aging:
questions.rationale: Aging tends to lower lymphocytes and alter immunoglobulins, decreasing resistance to infection.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Immune system (PDF p. 4)
questions.quote: Decreased resistance to infection and disease

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: To prevent pressure injuries in a bedridden older adult, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Frequent repositioning and pressure-redistributing surfaces prevent injury; massaging bony prominences and donut rings are no longer recommended.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 1 Hygiene and skin care (PDF p. 6)
questions.quote: Change position frequently. Loss of subcutaneous supporting tissues makes the skin sensitive to pressure.
